title: Tactical squad subdues man swinging sword
article: Police met a street-smart shogun early yesterday in Brampton -- and it took nine plastic bullets and five large cans of pepper spray before the sword-wielding man gave himself up.

Police were told that a man removed an ornamental sword from a friend's house early yesterday morning, threatened his friend and then took off on a bicycle with the one-metre blade slung over his back.
When a Peel Regional Police officer encountered a man carrying a sword, the man went into a samurai position and swung the blade several times. When the officer drew his gun, the man fled.

The confrontation continued with members of a police tactical squad. Police spokesman Constable Harry Tam said the man was shot with a total of nine Arwen plastic bullets -- one alone is considered quite painful -- but continued to brandish his sword.
Five cans of pepper spray -- the squad members carry the industrial size -- were then loosed at the 30-year-old man until finally, burning and sore, he surrendered.

"We must have tired him out somehow," Constable Tam said yesterday. He added it was lucky that members of the tactical squad dealt with the man, because they have more options for dealing with an armed person.
Constable Tam did not know whether the man was under the influence of drugs. But he said the suspect will undergo a psychiatric assessment.
Ucal Roy Lauzon, 30, of no fixed address, is charged with possession of a dangerous weapon and two counts of assault with a weapon.
